gate.reason: Two human calls, neither of them authority — `architecture.md` puts the module list in the tree's hands, so plan does not need a Decision to name `src/lock.rs`. (1) Sequencing and cost: a behavior-neutral ~2089-line move whose fence spans 63 existing files (16 `src/`, 42 `tests/it/`, `drift.rs`, and four re-blessed `ts-rs` bindings) beside the new `src/lock.rs` can share a wave with nothing, so it runs alone against a drained queue and buys churn against no test that could go red — whether to buy it at all is the human's. (2) Where the row→model lifts at the codec's tail land — `nested_members_from_rows` 6273 over `embedded_member_from_row` 6287, `requirement_from_row` 6310, `clause_from_row` 6338, `edges_from_declarations` 6355 over `edge_column` 6384, `mention_edges_from_declarations` 6395, `import_edges_from_doc` 6413: recommended answer is beside the model type they produce — `compose`/`graph`/`extract`, which is where `compose::clause_from_row` (407) already lives and what `drift::clause_from_row`'s thin delegation to it already implies — leaving `lock.rs` a codec with no model dependency. A ruling the other way (the lifts ride the codec) is one word in this entry.

new.description: The flat module (`architecture.md`, "The tree stays flat": a split lands as a new flat module) owning the lock declaration codec moved from `src/drift.rs` 4338-6426 — its section banner (4338-4340), `Declarations` (4361) and every `*Row` type, their `*_table`/`*_from_table` TOML round-trip pairs, the column readers (`req_str` 5342, `opt_str` 5347, `opt_table` 5409), `LockRowError` (719)/`RowError`, and the read/parse door (`read_lock_document` 5177, `read_declarations` 5214, `read_engine` 5231, `engine_from_doc` 5241, `parse_declarations` 5257, `declarations_from_doc` 5279). A move, not a rewrite: no signature, no behavior, no row column changes, and `drift` imports it rather than re-exporting it — one door per name, never two (`engineering.md`, "An export earns its consumer"). One byte of prose is not verbatim: `Declarations`'s doc (4353) names `GATE-READ-LOCK-DEMOLITION` as "next in the chain", a tag retired at ce61d85c — the clause goes, the sentence keeping the fact that `import`'s extraction still writes this family for the `check` path it feeds.
